description: Turn the data-specific outputs into reusable TEMPLATES plus a callable template-maker API. Each report type gets its own template that receives a schema instance (from FEAT-003) and renders the styled report; static chrome (headings, TOTAL row labels, column headers, ministry banner) lives in the template, data is filled in. Templates are named by level + purpose (e.g. council_top_10_students.html) accounting for private/overall/government variants where structure differs. Expose a Python API: supply data -> get HTML back -> use directly (.html) or convert to PDF and get the PDF. Depends on FEAT-002 (colour/elastic CSS) and FEAT-003 (schemas + extractor).
steps: Choose a templating mechanism consistent with the codebase. The existing html_out.py builds HTML with Python string assembly and a shared DOC_CSS + StylePool. Prefer reusing that machinery (no new heavy dependency): implement each template as a Python renderer function/class that takes a schema instance and emits the same clean semantic HTML+CSS the pipeline already produces, keeping table-layout:fixed + colgroup geometry and the elastic wrapping + competency colours from FEAT-002. If a text-based template engine is clearly better and a dependency is acceptable, jinja2 may be used, but the string-assembly approach that mirrors html_out.py is preferred to avoid drift. Whichever is chosen, the STATIC chrome (fixed headings, TOTAL labels, banner, column headers) is written once in the template and the DATA is injected.

Create one template per report type, named by level + purpose in a templates directory (e.g. src/sars/templates/ or a TEMPLATES registry). Examples following the user's convention: council_top_10_students.html / council_top_10_students_subjectwise, council_schools_rank (with overall/private/government variants where the structure differs), council_subjects_rank, council_wards_rank, region_schools_rank_overall, region_best_students_overall, region_best_students_subjectwise, region_overall_subjects_performance, region_school_rank_subject (EDK/English), region_district_performance, region_mock_mobility, school_result_slip. Map each report_type from FEAT-003's catalogue to its template. Where private/overall/government share structure, use one template parameterised by variant; only split into separate templates when the structure genuinely differs.

Implement the template-maker API in a clearly named module (e.g. src/sars/template_maker.py) exposing callables such as: `render_html(report_type, data) -> str` (returns the HTML string), `render_pdf(report_type, data, out_path=None) -> Path|bytes` (renders HTML then WeasyPrint to PDF, returning the path or bytes), and a convenience `make(data) -> str` that infers the report type from the schema instance's type. Each template has its own data shape (the FEAT-003 schema). Document each function with the exact data shape it expects.

Wire the competency background colour into the templates via the FEAT-002 competency module so the colour is DETERMINISTIC from the competency band/GPA in the data (not stored per-cell). Keep the rest of the styling as recovered.

Provide an end-to-end demonstration path: for at least one document per level (council, region, school), extract data (FEAT-003) -> feed to the matching template via the API -> render HTML and PDF -> confirm the produced PDF still passes `verify` against the reference (text similarity 100%, glyphs identical) and looks correct in a compare image. This proves the templated path reproduces the report from data alone.
Optionally add a CLI subcommand (e.g. `sars template --only "<name>"`) that runs the data->template->HTML/PDF path so it is exercisable from the command line.

Record in findings: the list of template names and which report_type/variant each serves, the API surface (function signatures + data shape per template), and the verification result for the demonstrated documents.
acceptance_criteria: A template exists per report type, named by level+purpose (e.g. council_top_10_students...), with private/overall/government handled as variants where structure matches and separate templates only where it differs.
Static chrome (headings, TOTAL labels, banner, column headers) lives in the template; all variable content comes from the schema data.
A callable API renders HTML from supplied data and can convert that HTML to PDF and return it (path or bytes); each template documents its expected data shape.
Competency background colour is applied deterministically from the competency band/GPA via the FEAT-002 mapping inside the templated output.

For at least one council, one region and one school document, the data->template->PDF path produces a PDF that passes verify against the reference (100% text similarity, glyphs identical) and matches the reference in a compare image.
verification: . .venv/bin/activate && python -c "from sars import template_maker; print('api ok')"
findings: Templates implemented as Python renderers in src/sars/templates/ (base, schools_rank, best_students, best_students_subjectwise, subjects_rank, school_result_slip, generic), registered in RENDERERS by report_type with TEMPLATE_NAMES giving level+purpose names. Added best_students_subjectwise as its own template: the subjectwise layout genuinely differs (MARKS/GRADE/COMPETENCY per subject vs AGGT/DIVISION/DETAILED SUBJECTS). API in src/sars/template_maker.py: render_html(report_type, data)->str, render_pdf(report_type, data, out_path=None)->Path|bytes, make(data)->str. CLI: `sars template [--only NAME]` writes output/template_html + output/template_pdf. Competency background applied deterministically via sars.competency (never stored). Major extraction fixes were required for the templated path to carry real data: (1) _main_table_group replaces _largest_table so a report continued across pages is captured whole and headers are read from the richest header band (previously a continuation page was picked, breaking column mapping and dropping pages 2+); (2) best-students extraction is now header-driven instead of using fixed column indices, covering all four council/region x overall/subjectwise layouts; (3) _group_totals no longer collapses repeated TOTAL labels, which had discarded the district report's government and private totals; (4) _titled_table_sections captures section headings printed as free-standing text above each block (subject names); (5) GenericTabularReport gained sections so blocks with differing column counts are all kept. Audit: no value lost 6/19, mean document similarity 97.26% (was 2/19 and 37.42%). Conversion path unchanged: 19/19 pass, 100% text similarity. Remaining gaps recorded in README: top-ten per-block headings not in data, school slip summary captions + 7 figures, and an apostrophe glyph difference on 3 documents.
